headline: Nasdaq-100 weekend halt: Tail stays low after Friday's record probe was fully retraced, while a long end near multi-decade highs, triple-digit Brent and firming Gulf escalation rhetoric keep Stress elevated
body:
Every hour of this published window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt. Index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, about ten hours after the final published slot, so there is no tradeable session in which sustained mean-reversion failure could occur. That, not benign structure, is why Tail is held at 3 to 5 across all 24 hours and every hour maps to EA_ON and green.

The last observable price path is Friday's session. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% and a record close, after probing an intraday record of 31,017.53 and then giving back roughly 210 points to finish near the session low of 30,737.07. A completed retracement of that size is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure this framework treats as Tail evidence. The VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% on a 15.30 to 16.24 range, so there is no observed volatility expansion to carry into the weekend either.

The session was driven by a soft September employment report: 29,000 jobs added against roughly 90,000 expected, unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1%, and average hourly earnings at 0.1% month over month and 3.0% year over year. Bond traders cut October rate-hike odds to the mid-teens from roughly 64% a week earlier. Technology led, with Nvidia briefly at an intraday record of $237.87 on a market capitalisation near $5.72 trillion, and Tesla up about 4% on 486,532 third-quarter deliveries against a 463,000 consensus.

The rate channel is less supportive than the equity close implies, and this run resolves a conflict left open by the previous assessment. The Federal Reserve H.15 release records the 2-year at 4.78%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61% on 1 October. The quote feed puts the 10-year about four basis points higher into Friday's close, near 5.28%, with the 2-year at 4.84% and the 30-year at 5.61%, after the 10-year had earlier in the week exceeded 5.34%, its highest since 2002. Read together, the official release and the Friday quote are consistent: the post-payroll bond rally reported immediately after the release faded into the close, so the long end did not confirm the equity advance. That unresolved cross-asset conflict is scored as a Stress and Confidence input rather than as Tail evidence.

Energy and geopolitics remain the standing Stress channels. Brent trades near $102.25, up about 7.1% on the month and 58.5% on the year, with the G7 releasing up to 100 million barrels of reserves over four months and a rebound in Persian Gulf flows offsetting part of the upward pressure. Regional crude exports have recovered toward about 21.8 million barrels a day against 23.3 million before the war, while refined-product flows through Hormuz remain far below pre-war levels and transit counts stay inconsistent across sources. A Sunday OPEC+ online meeting of seven core members, with a separate ministerial monitoring review, is reported to be likely to hold November production targets unchanged; its exact time was not independently confirmed for this run.

The geopolitical read is genuinely two-sided. A Tehran source said on Saturday that Iran is preparing for a major round of fighting and that the door to diplomacy has not closed, with the USS Theodore Roosevelt en route as a third carrier strike group and recent talks producing no breakthrough after seven months of conflict. Iran has separately received an official U.S. response to its proposal to end the war, with the sides reported to agree on the needed steps but not their order, Tehran seeking asset and sanctions relief before a phased Hormuz reopening. Against that rhetoric, the Day 218 operational record reports no coalition strike on Iranian territory for a twenty-sixth consecutive period, no Iranian ballistic salvo for twenty-four days and no drone attack for twenty-eight days, the longest such intervals of the resumed war, alongside a crude tanker struck by an unidentified projectile about four nautical miles off Oman. Under this framework all of that raises Stress and bears on Confidence; it cannot raise Tail while there is no session in which a pathological path could develop.

Confidence is 86 and eases to 79 across the window. The verified evidence set is strong: index level and session range, the VIX, the official H.15 yields reconciling with the Friday quote feed, Brent, the payroll detail, the OPEC+ expectation and a dated operational report. The decline reflects Friday's evidence ageing across a weekend in which no new price path can be observed, not thin sourcing. The shared Finviz context file was not usable for this run: its collection status is partial and its collection time of 29 September is roughly four days old, far outside the 90-minute freshness window, so it was disregarded and the assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

Dominant mode is recorded as normal throughout, describing an orderly two-way close followed by a halted market rather than any directional regime. No danger window is published, because a narrow evidence-based window requires a tradeable session and none exists inside this horizon. The nearest scheduled U.S. releases, Monday's ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z and Wednesday's FOMC Minutes at 18:00Z, sit outside this window and are carried in the event calendar.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the back half of Friday's payroll session and the first fifteen hours of the weekend halt. Tail reached 25 and then 27 across the 13:30Z cash open as the index gapped higher and extended toward its intraday record, the only stretch of the window that produced an orange state. Once that advance stalled and price retraced roughly 210 points into a close near the session low, Tail fell back to 22 and held between 21 and 23 through the U.S. afternoon. After the 21:00Z futures halt it dropped to 14 and then decayed steadily to 3 by the final hour as the absence of a tradeable session removed the mean-reversion-failure mechanism. Stress fell from 79 at the cash open to 54 by the end of the window as volatility decayed, and dominant mode moved from trend-up during the opening extension to mixed and then normal once the halt began. Confidence stayed between 82 and 89 throughout. All 24 slots are backed by published Claude assessments and are reproduced here without hindsight revision.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt: index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, about ten hours beyond the final published slot. With no tradeable session there is no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure, so Tail is projected to hold between 3 and 5 and every hour maps to EA_ON and green; the small drift higher in the Sunday hours reflects unpriced information accumulating toward an eventual restart, not observed structure. Stress eases from 53 to a window trough of 50 overnight and then firms back to 57 by the final hour as unabsorbed weekend inputs accumulate: a Sunday OPEC+ online meeting expected to hold November targets unchanged, Saturday reports that Iran is preparing for a major round of fighting, a third carrier strike group en route, triple-digit Brent, and a long end that closed about four basis points higher despite a very weak payroll print. Every projected hour stays in the elevated Stress band. Confidence declines from 86 to 79, remaining in the high band, to reflect Friday's closing evidence ageing across a weekend in which no new price path can be observed and an unusable shared Finviz context file. Hour-specific notes mark the Friday session analogues, the official and quoted yield readings, the energy and Hormuz supply channel, the two-sided geopolitical file, the Sunday OPEC+ checkpoint and the Treasury supply stack; the nearest scheduled U.S. releases, Monday's ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z and Wednesday's FOMC Minutes at 18:00Z, sit outside this window and are carried in the event calendar.
